name: Sylvane Ferris
role: Partner in Ferris & Merrifield, managers of Roosevelt's Maltese Cross ranch
bio: Sylvane Ferris was a partner in Ferris & Merrifield, which the Cow Boy identified in June 1884 as managers of Theodore Roosevelt's ranch, later called the Chimney Butte or Maltese Cross ranch, about seven and a half miles up the river from Medora. In summer 1884 the partners bought a thousand head in Iowa, and their ranch became known for its dances and parties, including Thanksgiving 1885. In January 1886 he and W. H. Merrifield went to Chicago at Roosevelt's invitation, and in October 1886 Roosevelt turned the Elkhorn brand over to Ferris & Merrifield, with the Maltese Cross kept as the main brand. In December 1886 the paper named him as a witness to the branding of two steers at the center of the case against George Myers.
